Hey! Your PR title `write.ts coerce JSON objects to strings` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix

- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks

I think the discussion about the system prompts needs to acknowledge the rapid improvements in model intelligence and capabilities that has occurred in just the past four months. Gemini 3.1 has had a massive improvement in reasoning capabilities compared to 3.0, which was already very strong, and substantially improved over 2.5.  

I've noticed often that Gemini models seem to perform poorly in OpenCode, with better quality analysis and reporting in the Gemini web app. This makes sense given that the Gemini.txt is over 7 months old.

The OpenCode system prompts are stale and outmoded, not keeping pace with the models. 

It doesn't much matter if they were created to be tailored to the models, if the models they were tailored are no longer relevant.

One reason I totally abandoned oh-my-opencode was the system prompts for agents and hook system was poorly constructed, and basically made smart models like Opus 4.5 act very stupid.

I suspect something similar is occurring with OpenCode's system prompts. Both, because they're stale/outdated, and because they focus myopically on coding. Today's models are much more intelligent, and trained well enough to code that I don't think they need the hand-holding they required 6 months ago. They need to be focused on using coding as just another tool in the problem-solving toolbox. 

An Opus 4.6 analysis of the OpenCode v1.2.10 git history finds:

System Prompt Staleness: Git-Proven

| File | Source Product | Last Substantive Change | Staleness |
|------|--------------|------------------------|-----------|
| gemini.txt | Gemini CLI | 2025-07-15 (created, NEVER modified) | 7+ months |
| qwen.txt | Claude Code (stripped) | 2025-07-29 (created, NEVER modified) | 7 months |
| beast.txt | GitHub Copilot | 2025-08-07 | 6.5 months |
| copilot-gpt-5.txt | GitHub Copilot | 2025-08-12 | 6 months |
| anthropic-20250930.txt | Claude Code snapshot | 2025-09-30 (frozen time-capsule) | 5 months |
| anthropic.txt | Claude Code | 2025-10-25 | 4 months |
| codex_header.txt | Codex CLI | 2026-01-20 (6-line tweak) | ~1 month |
| trinity.txt | New OpenCode template | 2026-02-06 | ~2 weeks |

I came to this Issues thread because after spending the past month carefully constructing sophisticated prompts for my Agentic Collaboration Framework and it's subsystems, I wondered if the OpenCode system prompts were helping or hindering, or if my prompts were duplicative of existing instruction.

What I found was the OpenCode system prompts seem to be in a sorry state. That many of the instructions limit the intelligence and autonomy of today's models. 

I can probably just load my ACF agents grounded in core ACF SPEC docs and point them at this system prompt problem, and say 'please fix' and produce superior system prompts. But without model specific data on current models, the prompts will be generalized. 

What's needed is to create a solid foundational template for OpenCode system prompts. Then develop a methodology and process to keep the system prompts updated by collecting performance data from community-members session data, extract insights from it, and apply it to the system prompts. The infrastructure is in place to support this. What's missing is OpenCode maintainers embracing their leadership role and organizing community members.

## Improvements

1. **No SSE/reactive updates.** The client polls a REST endpoint every 5s. This means the Web client would need to independently implement the same polling loop. Using the existing SSE event bus, both TUI and Web would get updates automatically through `sync.data`.
2. **No diff detection.** Every 5s poll returns the full panel list, even if nothing changed. Server-side diffing would only broadcast changes, reducing SSE traffic.
3. **No user-configurable ordering.** Panels appear in whatever order plugins register them. A `widget` key in `opencode.json` would let users reorder or hide widgets via config.
4. **No content format flexibility.** Items are strictly `label: string, value?: string` — you can't render a multi-line git diff, a markdown table, or freeform text. Supporting freeform `content` with `format: "text" | "markdown"` would cover more use cases.
5. **No widget limits or guardrails.** No max panels per plugin, no content size limits, no throttling. A buggy plugin could register unlimited panels.
6. **No ID namespacing.** Panel `id` is a bare string — two plugins could collide on `"status"`.
7. **No cleanup on unmount.** The `setInterval` is cleaned up via `onCleanup`, but there's no `dispose` hook for plugin-level teardown.
8. **No overlap guard.** The 5s `setInterval` doesn't check if the previous fetch completed. Slow responses could stack up.
9. **TUI only.** No Web implementation.

+1 on this. I've been hitting the same limitation daily — managing multiple projects means I need to find and resume sessions across all directories, not just the current one.

## Current state

`opencode session list` only shows sessions for the current working directory. `opencode -s <id>` works for resuming any session, but there's no way to **discover** sessions from other projects without manually querying the SQLite DB.

## Proposed CLI additions

```bash
# List all sessions globally (cross-project), sorted by last updated
opencode session list --global

# Full-text search across session content
opencode session search "amplitude API" --global

# Combined: list + filter by project path
opencode session list --global --directory "~/Projects/my-app"
```

### Why `--global`?

The default (current directory only) is the right default — it's what you want 90% of the time. But power users working across multiple projects need a way to find "that session where I debugged the auth flow last week" without remembering which directory it was in.

### Why `session search`?

Session titles are auto-generated and often not descriptive enough to find what you need. Being able to search message content (the `part` table with `json_extract(data, '$.type') = 'text'`) would make sessions actually discoverable.

## Working proof of concept

I built shell functions that query `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` directly as a workaround. They work well, but this belongs in the core CLI:

```bash
# Lists all sessions across all projects with title, date, folder, and session ID
oc-sessions() {
  local limit=${1:-20}
  sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
    "SELECT s.id, s.title, s.directory,
       strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M', datetime(s.time_updated/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime'))
     FROM session s WHERE s.parent_id IS NULL
     ORDER BY s.time_updated DESC LIMIT $limit;" \
  | while IFS='|' read -r sid title dir ts; do
      echo "  ${title:0:50}"
      echo "    $ts  ${dir/#$HOME/\~}"
      echo "    opencode -s $sid"
      echo
    done
}

# Full-text search across session message content
oc-search() {
  sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
    "SELECT s.title, p.session_id, json_extract(p.data, '$.text')
     FROM part p JOIN session s ON p.session_id = s.id
     WHERE p.data LIKE '%$1%' AND json_extract(p.data, '$.type') = 'text'
     ORDER BY p.time_created DESC LIMIT ${2:-10};"
}
```

Output looks like:

```
  1   Amplitude MCP setup and data analysis
        02-24 15:48  _sandbox/amplitude-mcp
        opencode -s ses_3757e6cbafferGgDFz54FXwRWF

  2   Blog layout and style bugfix
        02-24 15:47  operations/content/Blog
        opencode -s ses_371eac738ffev4hxJfa1h4Gszb
```

Happy to contribute a PR if the team agrees on the CLI API shape.
